chunks: An oath is of two types. One of them is that a man swears concerning something he is not obligated to do, so he swears that he will do that thing; or he swears concerning what he is obligated to do, then expiation is due upon him if he does not do it.

And the other is of three aspects: among them is that for which a man is rewarded if he swears falsely; among them is that for which there is no expiation upon him and no reward for him; and among them is that for which there is no expiation, and the punishment in it is entering the Fire.

As for that for which a man is rewarded if he swears falsely and for which expiation is not binding upon him, it is that a man swears for the deliverance of a Muslim person or the protection of his property from an aggressor who transgresses against him, whether a thief or other than him.

And as for that in which there is no expiation upon him and no reward for him, it is that a man swears upon something and then finds what is better than the oath, so he leaves the oath and returns to that which is better.

And as for that whose punishment is entering the Fire, it is that a man swears concerning the wealth of a Muslim man or concerning his right unjustly. This is a perjurious oath that necessitates the Fire, and there is no expiation upon him for it in this world.

key_terms.اَلنَّارِ: the Fire, meaning hellfire as punishment
key_terms.اَلْكَفَّارَةُ: the required expiation for breaking a binding oath
key_terms.يَمِينٌ غَمُوسٌ: a deeply sinful false oath that plunges one into sin and punishment

ai.seo_question: What are the different types of oaths in Islam, and when do they require expiation or lead to sin?
ai.summary: This hadith classifies oaths into different legal and moral categories, distinguishing between those that require expiation, those excused due to a greater good, and those that are grave sins. It emphasizes the protection of Muslim life and property, while strongly condemning false oaths used to usurp another person's wealth or rights.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4297 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"An oath is of two types. One type is when a man swears upon something that he is not obligated to do, yet he swears that he will do it.
The other type is when he swears upon something that he is obligated to do; in this case, if he does not fulfill it, he must offer expiation.

The second type has three categories. One of them is an oath for which a man will be rewarded if he swears falsely, another for which there is neither expiation nor reward, and the third for which there is no expiation but the punishment is entering the Fire.

As for the oath for which a man will be rewarded if he swears falsely and for which no expiation is required, it is when a person swears to protect the life of a Muslim or his property from an oppressor or a thief or anyone who intends harm.

As for the oath for which there is neither expiation nor reward, it is when a person swears upon something but later finds an option that is better than his oath, so he leaves the oath and chooses what is better.

And as for the oath whose punishment is entering the Fire, it is when a man swears falsely to take the wealth or rights of another Muslim unjustly. This is a 'Ghamus' oath, which necessitates the Fire, and there is no expiation for it in this world."
